claim: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) released its Food Guide Pyramid in 1992 (Home and Garden Bulletin No. 252). It placed the grains group — bread, cereal, rice, and pasta — at the base as the largest tier, recommending 6 to 11 servings per day, more than any other food group.

sources.label: USDA, 'The Food Guide Pyramid' (Home and Garden Bulletin No. 252, 1992)
sources.quote: The Pyramid recommends eating 6 to 11 servings of grain products each day; several should be whole-grain servings.
sources.clip_status: error: source is a direct-download PDF — no HTML page to clip; quote verified against the USDA bulletin PDF text

sources.label: Cole Soiney / @rant.board, Instagram reel DZJJvUbtJ2g (June 3, 2026) — surfacing source

notes: Year (1992) and the 6-11 grain-servings-at-base figure verified against USDA primary material. The reel's gloss that this told Americans grains were 'your most beneficial food group' is a fair reading of the base-of-pyramid, most-servings placement. The reel misdates it '1992' correctly in one breath but the on-screen board elsewhere reads loosely; the primary date stands at 1992 (superseded by MyPyramid in 2005 and MyPlate in 2011).
